findings.title: Honor client-specific view denials before granting all-clients view
findings.body: The no-argument canView() returns true for a view grant on the all-clients resource. Calling it here immediately authorizes every client without evaluating that client's resource. Consequently, an all-clients view grant combined with a client-specific negative view permission still allows the caller to view the explicitly denied client. The early bypass should be limited to role-based access; fine-grained access must evaluate the client-specific permission before falling back to all-clients permissions.

findings.title: Return real client IDs for all-clients permissions
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() creates a synthetic resource with type Clients and name "Clients", so findByType() includes it. When an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, this method adds "Clients" to the result rather than the IDs of authorized clients. For example, an all-clients map-roles grant returns no real client IDs unless separate client resources also exist, causing consumers that filter available clients or client roles using this set to omit authorized clients. Handle the synthetic resource separately and return actual client IDs while respecting client-specific overrides.

findings.title: Restore the login client's secret after testing rotation
findings.body: This test rotates and then invalidates the old secret of myclient, which is also the OAuth client used by the injected realmAdminClient. No cleanup restores that secret; the @AfterEach method only removes permissions. Cached access tokens can hide the problem temporarily, but subsequent token acquisition or refresh still uses the original configured secret and fails with invalid_client, making the tests token-expiration/order dependent. Use a separate managed client for secret operations or restore the original secret in cleanup.

findings.title: Document requireView methods as enforcement methods
findings.body: The new Javadoc says requireView() returns true when canView() succeeds, but requireView() is void and signals denied access by throwing ForbiddenException. The same incorrect return-value contract is documented for requireViewClientScopes(). These comments should describe the exception behavior, as the other require methods do, rather than promise a nonexistent boolean result.
